title: Self-Augmented Preference Optimization: Off-Policy Paradigms for Language Model Alignment

contributions.purpose: Remove the dependence of preference-optimization alignment (DPO/ORPO) on static, pre-collected paired preference data, so alignment can work with only prompts and chosen responses.
contributions.mechanism: Self-Augmented Preference Optimization (SAPO): a self-play paradigm that autonomously generates rejected responses via segment-level teacher-forcing supervision (truncate a chosen response at a random point and let the model regenerate the rest as a negative), combined with an off-policy pipeline using an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) model plus a first-in-first-out replay buffer to dynamically update training data.
contributions.evaluation: LLaMA3-8B and Mistral-7B trained on Distilabel-Capybara, 8 H100 GPUs; evaluated on Open LLM Leaderboard, IFEval, MT-Bench, AlpacaEval 2.0. ORPO-based LLaMA reaches Open LLM Leaderboard avg 67.36 and MT-Bench avg 7.45; SAPO matches or surpasses DPO/ORPO and outperforms self-play SPIN.
contributions.source_quote: To overcome this limitation, we introduce Self-Augmented Preference Optimization (SAPO), an effective and scalable training paradigm that does not require existing paired data. Building on the self-play concept, which autonomously generates negative responses, we further incorporate an off-policy learning pipeline to enhance data exploration and exploitation.

contributions.purpose: Show that segment-level negative generation and off-policy machinery (EMA reference + replay buffer) actually drive SAPO's gains, and identify optimal settings.
contributions.mechanism: Ablations over training paradigm (on-policy vs off-policy), reference-model update strategy (fixed vs policy-ref vs ema-ref), number of rejected responses per prompt (1/4/8), segment token length (64/256), and training epochs.
contributions.evaluation: ema-ref update strategy gives best performance; on-policy sampling degrades IFEval and Open LLM Leaderboard; increasing rejected responses from 1 to 4 to 8 reduces performance (overfitting); segment length 256 > 64; MT-Bench peaks at 4 epochs (chosen setting).
contributions.source_quote: In Table 3, our ablation study of the LLaMA-3-8B model using the ORPO algorithm showed that on-policy sampling led to notable declines in performance on benchmarks like IFEval and the Open LLM Leaderboard.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Building on the self-play concept, which autonomously generates negative responses, we further incorporate an off-policy learning pipeline to enhance data exploration and exploitation.
Furthermore, we integrate an EMA model and a replay buffer-techniques well-established in RL-to facilitate standard off-policy training.

In the training stage, we randomly select a batch of tuples from the replay buffer and employ typical preference learning methods, such as DPO (Rafailov et al.,2023) and ORPO (Hong et al., 2024), to train the current policy.

notes: Negative/mixed results explicitly reported: SAPO underperforms LLaMA-based SPIN on single-turn AlpacaEval 2.0 tasks (authors argue AlpacaEval is single-turn while they trained on multi-turn Capybara, and recommend MT-Bench as the fairer metric). Ablation shows increasing the number of rejected responses per prompt (1->4->8) hurts performance (overfitting). Extends DPO/ORPO/SPIN by grafting off-policy RL machinery (EMA + replay buffer) onto self-play.
